Subject: Re: Quick Q: your 'we do not train on customer data' statement vs. debug snapshots

Hi Alex — thanks for surfacing this. Short answer: we do not train any of our models on customer traffic for hosted, dedicated, or private deployments unless a customer explicitly opts in via a signed agreement. That commitment is documented here: https://docs.redwood.com/security/no-train-guarantee (shared below).

To address the debug snapshot question specifically:
- What they are: temporary captures of request/response payloads and a tiny associated runtime state used strictly for reproducing incidents (e.g., KV cache state + request metadata).
- Retention: by default snapshots are retained for up to 7 days in hosted environments, and up to 14 days if the customer has enabled extended debug retention (rare; usually by explicit support request).
- Use: snapshots are accessible only to a limited incident-response role, stored encrypted-at-rest, and are never included in any training corpus or model update pipeline. We maintain an internal policy and audit trail to ensure no snapshot data flows into model training; this is enforced through pipeline gating and manual sign-offs in repo histories.
- Opt-out: customers can disable automatic snapshot collection for their account or request immediate deletion after an incident (support ticket). For Private deployments, the default is no automatic upload of snapshots to Redwood-managed storage; customers can choose to enable collection for operational convenience.

I've attached a short explainer (redwood-debug-snapshots-explainer.pdf) you can share with procurement, and a sample request log you attached so they see the minimal fields we capture.

Below is a condensed FAQ you can paste into an SOW/email to legal. Let me know if you want a formal signed clause.

—Olga

Subject: Re: Quick Q: your 'we do not train on customer data' statement vs. debug snapshots

Thanks — good callout on the nuance. Final wording for external/legal: 

1) Non-training guarantee: Redwood does not use customer data to train, fine-tune, or improve production model weights for any customer account unless explicit, documented opt-in is signed. This applies across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes.

2) Operational telemetry vs. debug snapshots: we do export aggregate telemetry (numeric metrics such as request counts, token histograms, latency percentiles) that are permanently decoupled from raw text payloads and used to optimize system behavior (e.g., batching heuristics). Those aggregates are strictly numeric and cannot be used to reconstruct customer content.

3) Debug snapshots: temporary captures of request/response and limited runtime state used solely for incident reproduction. Snapshots are retained by default: Hosted = 7 days, Dedicated = 14 days (unless customer requests a different window). In Private deployments there is no automatic export to Redwood-managed storage; retention is controlled by the customer's configuration.

4) Training pipeline exclusion: debug snapshots and any raw request payloads are explicitly excluded from model training and dataset-building pipelines by policy and by pipeline checks. We also have audit logs for every dataset ingest and a manual approval step before any dataset is ever used in training.

5) Opt-out and deletion: customers can disable snapshot collection or request immediate deletion via support@redwood.com (include account id). Deletion requests are audited and time-stamped; we provide confirmation when completed.

- If you need a contract clause, Legal (Maya) can draft standard language; we can iterate.
